india.name: India
india.summary: A fast-growing single-malt region where tropical heat drives rapid oak extraction; expressions range from unpeated sherried malts to boldly peated ones.

indian-malt.phenol: unpeated in the standard expressions (Rampur); Amrut's peated lines differ — see the peated profile
indian-malt.dilution: Typically 43–50% depending on the expression; the 50% bottlings take a few drops of water well
indian-malt.ice: A single cube is workable for casual drinking; detail shows best without it
indian-malt.ageing: Often 4–12 years; tropical heat accelerates oak extraction relative to cooler climates (widely reported, e.g. Amrut's own maturation notes)
indian-malt.expect: Rich and fast-matured: bold oak, tropical fruit and spice even at young age statements.

style.label: Indian malt (unpeated) · Tropical richness
style.method: Scottish-style pot distillation; ex-bourbon casks finished in sherry casks (Rampur Double Cask, Rampur Distillery, Uttar Pradesh (Radico Khaitan))
style.effect: Sustained tropical heat speeds the spirit's interaction with oak, concentrating flavor faster than in Scotland — the mechanism is physical, not a shortcut to identical complexity

bottles.name: Rampur Double Cask
bottles.note: Unpeated, sherry-finished Himalayan-region malt (Rampur Distillery, Uttar Pradesh (Radico Khaitan))

indian-peated-malt.phenol: peated — Amrut Fusion marries peated and unpeated barley (Amrut's published notes describe pronounced peat)
indian-peated-malt.dilution: Amrut Fusion is bottled at 50% ABV; water tames the heat and opens the smoke
indian-peated-malt.ice: Ice tends to close down the peat and oak detail; prefer water if diluting
indian-peated-malt.ageing: Fusion's components vary; check the batch — no single age window covers it
indian-peated-malt.expect: Bold and smoky: pronounced sweet peat over tropical fruit and heavy oak.

style.label: Indian peated malt · Bold sweet smoke
style.method: Peated and unpeated barley married after separate distillation (Amrut Fusion)
style.effect: Peat reads sweeter and bolder against the ripe fruit profile of tropical maturation

bottles.name: Amrut Fusion
bottles.note: Peated-plus-unpeated marriage at 50% ABV; pronounced sweet smoke (Amrut)

identity.terrain: Varied; key distilleries near Bangalore and the Himalayas
influences: Amrut (Bangalore) pioneered Indian single malt exports from 2004
Rampur (Himalayan foothills) offers a cooler-maturation contrast

Heat-driven maturation is the region's defining variable; note that much whisky sold in India is molasses-based and would not qualify as whisky in the EU — single malts like Amrut and Rampur are grain-based

why.cause: Sustained high warehouse temperatures in the tropics
why.effect: Oak extraction and evaporation run faster than in cool climates — maturation is accelerated, though it does not simply replicate Scotch's slower development (Amrut maturation notes; widely reported industry observation)

why.cause: High evaporation losses in hot, humid conditions
why.effect: Concentration of the remaining spirit — the famous 'angel's share' trade-off, one reason Indian malts can taste mature young

taiwan.name: Taiwan
taiwan.summary: A fast-rising whisky region: Kavalan's Solist range has taken multiple World Whiskies Awards titles since 2015.

taiwanese-malt.serve: Neat with a few drops of water
taiwanese-malt.expect: Lush and fruity with wine-cask refinement: award-winning depth at remarkably young ages.

style.label: Taiwanese malt · Lush & wine-cask-influenced
style.method: Pot distillation in subtropical heat, heavy use of wine and sherry casks
style.effect: Heat plus wine-cask finishing creates mature depth at young age statements

bottles.name: Kavalan Solist Sherry
bottles.note: Cask-strength sherry bomb from the award magnet

bottles.name: Kavalan Classic
bottles.note: The accessible face of Taiwanese whisky

taiwanese-malt.dilution: Kavalan Solist editions are cask strength (around 55–58%); most drinkers prefer some water, but the strength is the point — dilute to your own taste
taiwanese-malt.ice: Many drinkers find the fruit shows best without ice; a small cube is workable

influences: King Car Group's 2005 entry into whisky
Multiple World Whiskies Awards since 2015

why.cause: Humid subtropical climate
why.effect: Fast maturation with rich extraction, like India but wine-cask focused

why.cause: Ambitious wine and sherry cask programs
why.effect: Distinguish a young industry with layered vinous flavors

england.name: England
england.summary: A whisky revival after a century-long hiatus: small craft distilleries making precise, spirit-driven malts.

english-malt.expect: Bright and spirit-led: young but precise, with wine-cask creativity.

style.label: English malt · Bright & craft-led
style.method: Small-batch pot distillation, often wine and ex-bourbon casks
style.effect: Craft-scale precision with cask creativity marks the revival

bottles.name: The English Whisky Co. Chapter 14
bottles.note: From England's first modern distillery (2006)

bottles.name: Cotswolds Single Malt
bottles.note: Wine-cask influenced and unfiltered

english-malt.ice: A cube is fine for the bright, young style

influences: No English whisky from ~1905 to 2006
Brewing-country heritage informs fermentation

why.cause: A century-long gap then craft-era restart
why.effect: Modern equipment and no legacy constraints: creative casks and yeast choices

why.cause: Premium English barley from brewing supply chains
why.effect: Excellent raw material for spirit-first styles

finland.name: Finland
finland.climate: Cold continental: long freezing winters, short warm summers
finland.summary: A young Nordic whisky country: malted-rye whisky from Kyrö and Finland's oldest single malts from Teerenpeli.

malted-rye.phenol: unpeated in the core Kyrö Malt; Wood Smoke and Peat Smoke editions are smoked
malted-rye.serve: Neat, with a splash of water, or in a rye cocktail
malted-rye.dilution: Kyrö's core range is bottled at 47.2% ABV; a little water softens the rye spice
malted-rye.ice: A large cube works; the spice survives it
malted-rye.ageing: Young by age statement; new American oak gives a lot of flavour quickly
malted-rye.expect: Spicy and bready: 100% malted rye gives rye-bread spice over vanilla from new oak.

style.label: Finnish malted rye · Spicy & bready
style.method: 100% malted Finnish rye, copper pot stills, mostly new American oak (Kyrö)
style.effect: All the rye is malted; malted rye is usually described as rounder and more bread-like than the raw rye in American mashbills

bottles.name: Kyrö Malt
bottles.note: The core 100% malted-rye whisky at 47.2%, matured in new American oak

bottles.name: Kyrö Oloroso
bottles.note: Malted rye with oloroso sherry casks alongside new oak and ex-bourbon

unpeated-malt.phenol: unpeated in the core range; the Savu edition is peated
unpeated-malt.serve: Neat; a drop of water opens the fruit
unpeated-malt.ice: A single cube is fine for casual drinking
unpeated-malt.ageing: The 10-year-old is the reference point; Kaski is a six-year-old sherry-cask malt
unpeated-malt.expect: Rounded Nordic malt: toffee and orchard fruit with a peppery, oily edge from bourbon and sherry casks.

style.label: Finnish single malt · Toffee & pepper
style.method: Pot-distilled local barley, bourbon and sherry casks (Teerenpeli)
style.effect: Sherry casks add dried fruit and toffee to an oily, peppery spirit

bottles.name: Teerenpeli 10
bottles.note: Bourbon and sherry casks: butterscotch, orchard fruit and pepper

bottles.name: Teerenpeli Kaski
bottles.note: Six years in sherry casks: brown sugar, raisin and spice

identity.setting: Cold continental climate with large seasonal swings
identity.terrain: Lakes, farmland and the Ostrobothnian plains
identity.soil: Glacial soils; rye has long been Finland's bread grain
influences: Teerenpeli (Lahti, 2002) is Finland's oldest single malt producer
Kyrö (Isokyrö, opened 2014) makes whisky and gin only from local rye

why.cause: 100% malted rye instead of a corn-led mashbill
why.effect: Rye spice without bourbon's corn sweetness, with a bready grain character

why.cause: New American oak for much of the rye
why.effect: Strong vanilla and toasted-oak flavour even at young ages

why.cause: Large swings between freezing winters and warm summers
why.effect: Cask interaction varies sharply by season; most maturation happens in the warm months

sweden.name: Sweden (High Coast)
sweden.climate: Subarctic coast: winters down to about -38°C, short summers
sweden.summary: Northern Swedish malt made at 63° north, often in small casks of several oak types, with peat used in part of the range.

lightly-peated-malt.phenol: lightly to moderately peated depending on the expression; Älv is unpeated
lightly-peated-malt.serve: Neat with a splash of water
lightly-peated-malt.dilution: Core range bottled at 46–50%; a few drops of water help
lightly-peated-malt.ice: Water shows more of the oak spice than ice
lightly-peated-malt.ageing: Young no-age-statement core range; small casks speed oak extraction
lightly-peated-malt.expect: Crisp and spicy northern malt: oak spice, juniper-like freshness and a light, woody smoke.

style.label: Swedish malt · Oak spice & light smoke
style.method: Pot-distilled malt, partly peated; first-fill bourbon, virgin oak and small 40-litre casks including Swedish and Hungarian oak (High Coast)
style.effect: Small casks and virgin oak give a lot of wood spice quickly; the peated share adds a light, ashy smoke

bottles.name: High Coast Timmer
bottles.note: The peated core bottling (46%): vanilla, custard and campfire ash

bottles.name: High Coast Hav
bottles.note: 48%, partly peated, small virgin-oak casks: clove, juniper and oak

bottles.name: High Coast Älv
bottles.note: Unpeated, first-fill bourbon (46%): green apple and vanilla

identity.setting: Northern Baltic coast at about 63° north
identity.terrain: The Ångermanälven river valley near the sea, a UNESCO-listed landscape
influences: Founded in 2010 as Box distillery; renamed High Coast in 2018
Mackmyra pioneered Swedish malt, though its ownership has been turbulent since 2024

why.cause: Extreme seasonal temperature swings
why.effect: Spirit is pushed into the wood in summer and pulled back in winter, so maturation is uneven through the year

why.cause: Small casks and virgin oak
why.effect: More wood contact per litre gives oak spice and vanilla at young ages

why.cause: Only part of the spirit is peated
why.effect: Smoke stays in the background rather than dominating

switzerland.name: Switzerland (Appenzell)
switzerland.summary: Grain distilling was banned in Switzerland until 1999; Säntis Malt answered by maturing whisky in old beer casks.

unpeated-malt.dilution: Edition Sigel is 40% and needs no water
unpeated-malt.ice: A cube suits the gentle house style
unpeated-malt.ageing: Mostly no age statement; older single casks appear occasionally
unpeated-malt.expect: Soft, malty Alpine whisky: honeyed barley and nutty oak from old beer casks.

style.label: Swiss beer-cask malt · Soft & malty
style.method: Malt whisky from a brewery, matured in old oak beer casks (Säntis Malt, Brauerei Locher)
style.effect: Long-used beer casks give little new oak flavour, so the malt stays in front

bottles.name: Säntis Malt Edition Sigel
bottles.note: The entry bottling at 40%, matured in old beer casks

bottles.name: Säntis Malt Edition Himmelberg
bottles.note: A 43% edition from the same beer-cask house

peated-malt.phenol: peated with high-altitude moor peat and smoked with alpine wood
peated-malt.serve: Neat with a few drops of water
peated-malt.dilution: Bottled at 52%; water opens it and softens the heat
peated-malt.ice: Water rather than ice keeps the smoke detail
peated-malt.expect: Smoky and alpine: peat and wood smoke together, at a strong 52%.

style.label: Swiss peated malt · Peat & alpine wood smoke
style.method: Barley dried with high-altitude moor peat and smoked with Appenzell wood, matured in old beer casks (Säntis Malt Edition Dreifaltigkeit)
style.effect: Wood smoke alongside peat gives a drier, campfire-like smoke rather than a medicinal one

bottles.name: Säntis Malt Edition Dreifaltigkeit
bottles.note: Peated and alpine-wood smoked, 52%; Jim Murray's European Whisky of the Year 2010

identity.setting: Appenzell, at the foot of the Alpstein massif
identity.soil: Limestone mountains; spring water from the Alpstein
influences: Distilling spirits from grain was banned until 1 July 1999
Brauerei Locher, a century-old brewery, began Säntis Malt in 1999 and released its first whisky in 2002

why.cause: A brewery making whisky after the 1999 law change
why.effect: Old beer casks were at hand and became the house signature

why.cause: Long-used beer casks rather than fresh bourbon or sherry wood
why.effect: Less vanilla and dried fruit from the wood; the malt itself stays in front

why.cause: Alpine wood smoke in the peated edition
why.effect: A drier, campfire-like smoke rather than the medicinal phenols of Islay peat

wales.name: Wales
wales.summary: Penderyn revived Welsh whisky in 2004 with an unusual still that makes a very light, high-strength spirit in one run.

unpeated-malt.phenol: unpeated in the core range; Penderyn also bottles a peated edition
unpeated-malt.dilution: Legend and Myth are 41%; the 46% bottlings take a drop of water
unpeated-malt.ice: The light spirit works well over ice
unpeated-malt.ageing: No age statement core range; Madeira-cask finishes are the house signature
unpeated-malt.expect: Light and fruity: a delicate spirit lifted by Madeira-cask sweetness.

style.label: Welsh single malt · Light & Madeira-sweet
style.method: Faraday still (a pot still with an attached column) producing spirit at about 92% ABV in one run, plus pot stills since 2015; bourbon casks, often Madeira-finished (Penderyn)
style.effect: Very high spirit strength strips out heavier compounds, giving a light spirit that takes on cask sweetness readily

bottles.name: Penderyn Legend
bottles.note: Bourbon-matured, Madeira-finished at 41%: light and fruity

bottles.name: Penderyn Madeira
bottles.note: The flagship Madeira finish at 46%

identity.setting: The edge of the Brecon Beacons (Bannau Brycheiniog), south Wales
influences: First bottle sold in 2004, on St David's Day
Additional distilleries opened in Llandudno (2021) and Swansea (2023)

why.cause: The Faraday still, a pot still with a fractionating column attached
why.effect: Spirit at about 92% ABV in one run, much lighter than double-distilled Scotch at around 70%

why.cause: Madeira wine casks for finishing
why.effect: Adds dried fruit and sweetness to a delicate base spirit

tasmania.name: Tasmania
tasmania.summary: Australia's whisky island: small-scale distilling was effectively banned until 1992, and its single casks have since won world titles.

unpeated-malt.serve: Neat with a few drops of water
unpeated-malt.dilution: Single casks are typically around 47.5%; a little water opens them
unpeated-malt.ageing: Single casks often 10–12 years or more; each cask differs
unpeated-malt.expect: Rich and oak-led: dried fruit and toasted oak from single casks, many of them ex-fortified-wine.

style.label: Tasmanian single cask · Rich & oak-led
style.method: Small-batch malt bottled cask by cask; American oak and French oak, including ex-tawny (Australian fortified wine) casks (Sullivans Cove)
style.effect: Single-cask bottling means each release shows one cask's character; fortified-wine casks add dried fruit and depth

bottles.name: Sullivans Cove French Oak
bottles.note: Single-cask French oak; a 2014 cask was the first non-Scotch, non-Japanese World's Best Single Malt

bottles.name: Sullivans Cove American Oak
bottles.note: Single-cask American oak; ex-tawny editions add dried fruit

lightly-peated-malt.phenol: a light touch of Tasmanian peat
lightly-peated-malt.ice: A cube is workable; the dessert-like fruit shows best without
lightly-peated-malt.ageing: No age statement; small casks speed maturation
lightly-peated-malt.expect: Dessert-like Tasmanian malt: plum pudding and toffee apple with a faint wisp of local peat.

style.label: Tasmanian malt · Fruity with a hint of peat
style.method: Double-distilled malt, small casks including ex-tawny, a little Tasmanian peat (LARK Classic Cask)
style.effect: Small fortified-wine casks give rich fruit quickly; local peat adds only a background wisp

bottles.name: LARK Classic Cask
bottles.note: The house benchmark at 43%: plum pudding, toffee apple and a hint of Tasmanian peat

identity.setting: Cool island south of mainland Australia
identity.terrain: Highlands, river valleys and the Coal River area near Hobart
identity.soil: Barley country with local peat bogs
influences: Bill Lark had the 1839 and 1901 distilling Acts amended in 1992, founding LARK
Sullivans Cove followed in 1994 on Hobart's waterfront

why.cause: Ex-tawny and other fortified-wine casks, often small
why.effect: Dried fruit, plum and toffee develop quickly and dominate the profile

why.cause: Single-cask bottling
why.effect: Each release can taste noticeably different; the cask matters more than the house

why.cause: Local Tasmanian peat used sparingly
why.effect: Earthy background smoke rather than Islay-style medicinal peat

israel.name: Israel
israel.climate: Hot Mediterranean: summers up to about 40°C and very humid
israel.summary: Fast, hot maturation on the Tel Aviv coast and at the Dead Sea, losing up to a quarter of each cask a year.

unpeated-malt.serve: Neat or with a splash of water
unpeated-malt.dilution: Classic is 46%; a few drops of water soften the pepper
unpeated-malt.ice: A cube is workable for casual drinking
unpeated-malt.ageing: About three years can be enough in this climate; no age statement on the core range
unpeated-malt.expect: Young but full: vanilla, honey and black pepper, with more weight than its age suggests.

style.label: Israeli single malt · Hot-climate fast maturation
style.method: Unpeated malted barley, double distilled in copper pot stills; ex-bourbon and shaved, toasted, re-charred ex-red-wine (STR) casks (Milk & Honey)
style.effect: Heat speeds the spirit's interaction with the cask, so the whisky tastes fuller at three years than a Scotch of the same age

bottles.name: Milk & Honey Classic
bottles.note: 46%, ex-bourbon and STR red-wine casks: vanilla, honey and black pepper

identity.setting: Mediterranean coast at Tel Aviv, plus maturation at the Dead Sea
identity.terrain: Coastal city and desert rift valley
identity.soil: Not site-specific; the climate is the defining variable
influences: Trial runs in 2014, first single malt released in 2017
Casks at the Dead Sea, around 50°C in summer, stay only about 18 months

why.cause: Summers around 40°C with high humidity
why.effect: Fast cask interaction: fuller-bodied whisky at a young age

why.cause: Angel's share of up to 25% a year, against about 2% in Scotland
why.effect: Long ageing is impractical; whiskies are bottled young by necessity

mexico.name: Mexico (Abasolo)
mexico.climate: High-altitude highland: warm days, cool nights
mexico.summary: Whisky from heritage Mexican corn, treated by nixtamalization as for tortillas, distilled at about 2,375 m.

heritage-corn.serve: Neat, on the rocks, or in cocktails
heritage-corn.ice: Works well over ice and in highballs
heritage-corn.ageing: No age statement; second-fill bourbon casks keep the oak in the background
heritage-corn.expect: Sweet and creamy: grilled sweetcorn, toasted tortilla and vanilla toffee, quite unlike bourbon.

style.label: Mexican heritage corn · Toasted & creamy
style.method: 100% cacahuazintle and heritage maize, nixtamalized, 120-hour fermentation, double distilled in copper pot stills, second-fill ex-bourbon casks (Abasolo)
style.effect: Nixtamalization (cooking corn with lime) gives the toasted-tortilla character; reused casks leave the corn in front

bottles.name: Abasolo El Whisky de México
bottles.note: 100% nixtamalized heritage corn at 43%: grilled sweetcorn, honey and vanilla toffee

identity.setting: Jilotepec, north of Mexico City, at about 2,375 m
identity.soil: Volcanic highland soils where heritage maize is grown
influences: Nixtamalization is a pre-Hispanic technique, still used for tortillas
Cacahuazintle is a large-kernelled indigenous maize

why.cause: Nixtamalization: cooking the corn in alkaline lime water
why.effect: Toasted, tortilla-like corn flavour that untreated bourbon corn doesn't have

why.cause: Double distillation in copper pot stills
why.effect: Pot stills keep more of the heavier compounds than a column, giving a creamier texture

why.cause: Second-fill ex-bourbon casks rather than new charred oak
why.effect: Less vanilla and char than bourbon; the corn character stays in front
